headline: The Model Found Its Biggest Edge And Lost It By One Point
paragraphs: Six games got graded, one got the shrug, and five of them produced six tickets at ten dollars apiece. The scoreboard: 2-4, down $21.82, an ROI of negative 36.4 percent against an expected win rate of 66.1 percent. The spread book went 2-3 for a loss of $11.82. The lone moneyline went 0-1. Sixty dollars in, thirty eight dollars and change out.

Akron at Massachusetts is the whole week in one line. The model saw a 9.9 point edge, the fattest number on the board, liked Massachusetts minus 3 at 77 percent, then doubled back and took the moneyline at minus 162 with 80 percent confidence. Akron won 34 to 33. Twenty dollars, one point, two tickets, zero defense available. Miami (OH) minus 9.5 at a modest 60 percent cashed 20 to 3 and nobody noticed.

One line moved all week, and it moved away. Zero percent drift toward the model, which is at least honest. Nine weeks graded for real leaves the season at 228-283-15 across 526 plays, down $608.41, an ROI of negative 11.6 percent, and a 44.6 percent hit rate against 60.7 percent expected. There is a 40-25-1 week worth $110.47 sitting in a drawer, graded after the fact, which is to say graded by a model that already knew the answers.
